claims.statement: ECShopX outbound third-party integrations follow a silent-skip invariant: clients check base-URL/credentials before each call and return a `fail_msg` map (or empty map/null) instead of throwing, so an unconfigured install produces no external traffic and business flows never fail on missing integration config. All integration base-urls ship empty in application.properties.

JushuitanOpenApiClient form-POSTs to `ecshopx.jushuitan.api-base-url` with params biz/app_key/access_token/timestamp/charset=utf-8/version=2 and md5(appSecret + assembled) sign; six method→path mappings (itemsku/upload, skumap/upload, inventory/query, orders/upload, orders/cancel, aftersales/upload); missing config, unknown method, or transport error all return a fail_msg map rather than throwing.

WdtErpOpenApiClient signs with a legacy epoch offset (epochSeconds - 1325347200), splits the app secret into `secretPart:salt` (sign = md5(secretPart + sortedKV + secretPart), salt sent as query param), sends the `X-Version-SDK: java-ecshopx` header, and reads platform credentials from `ecshopx.wdterp.*` @Value properties which are absent from application.properties — per-tenant WdtErpSetting Redis values win when present; all nine API method names are individually overridable via `ecshopx.wdterp.methods.*`.

On payment success, OrdersTradePaymentCallbackService publishes the snake_case trade row on three independent planes: dedicated ASYNC+REDIS events `event:systemlink:jushuitan_trade_finish` and `event:systemlink:wdt_erp_trade_finish`, plus the shared orders trade-finish event via `OrdersTradeFinishAfterCommitDispatchPublisher` (@Primary for event:291; bean `ordersTradeFinishDispatchPublisherOfflineCsv292` publishes event:292 for offline bank-transfer approval) which registers an after-commit TransactionSynchronization and publishes with DispatchOptions.eventDefaults() = SYNC mode so all listeners on that plane run in-process in @Order sequence once the payment transaction commits.

The SYNC trade-finish plane (event:291/event:292) carries registered listeners in @Order sequence: 77 `listener:orders.trade_finish_normal_order_pay_success_bridge` (marks mall orders paid and republishes `event:288` normal-order pay-success ASYNC+REDIS), 82 `listener:thirdparty.dm_crm.trade_finish`, 83 `listener:thirdparty.marketing_center.trade_finish_basics_order_pay`, 92 `listener:systemlink.trade_finish_send_ome`, 95 `listener:orders.listeners.TradeFinishCustomDeclareOrder` (WeChat customs).

`event:thirdparty:trade_refund_finish` is published SYNC and carries four sync listeners: Marketing Center push, DmCrm, Shuyun open-platform refund sync, and Shuyun trade re-sync (`shuyun.open_platform.refund_sync_on_trade_refund_finish` plus the trade_sync re-push).

The shared `event:systemlink:*` family (ome_trade_update, trade_refund, trade_aftersales, trade_aftersales_cancel, trade_aftersales_logi) carries multiple downstream listeners each — OME plus Marketing Center and/or SaasErp — published through ASYNC+REDIS fan-out publisher wrappers so one aftersales state change becomes one queued message per downstream rather than a serial blocking chain.

Optional outbound HTTP capabilities in ecshopx-third-party are port interfaces with two bean implementations: an HTTP impl registered by @ConditionalOnProperty(name="http-enabled", havingValue="true") and a NoOp registered by havingValue="false", matchIfMissing=true — so an unset key means NoOp and the NoOp returns an empty result. Gated keys include dm-crm.point-detail-list.http-enabled, dm-crm.update-member-info-by-mobile.http-enabled, dm-crm.setting-read.redis-enabled (true default, @Primary Redis read vs NoOp treating point integration as off), shuyun.member-modify/member-unbind.http-enabled, shopex-crm.sync-single-member.http-enabled, plus dada/shansong local-delivery clients.

DmCrm (达摩 Hope) HTTP services share the fixed base https://hope.demogic.com with /cgi-api workers, cache tokens in Redis `damo_token:{companyId}` (reused only while >1h validity remains, else /cgi-api/auth/get_token with appKey/appSecret from DmCrmSetting:{sha1(companyId)}), and the trade-finish orchestrator runs two phases — point change (guarded by isPointIntegrationOpen and dm_point_preid) and order sync (header+items with goods overlay) — swallowing all exceptions at log.debug so a Hope outage never breaks order flow.

MarketingCenterOpenApiSignedFormClient is the outbound twin of the inbound OpenAPI gateway: it reads the company's openapi_developer row (external_base_uri/external_app_key/external_app_secret), builds {data, timestamp 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss', app_key, version 1.0, method}, signs md5Upper(appSecret + assemble + appSecret), form-POSTs to {base}/api/openapi, and returns an empty map for every failure mode (missing developer row, missing external fields, non-2xx, unparseable body) so a marketing-center outage never breaks order flow.

PrismCoreHttpClient and PrismIshopexHttpClient share one sign contract (PrismIshopexHttpClient.produceSign): md5Upper(secret & METHOD & rawUrlEncode(path) & rawUrlEncode(headers) & rawUrlEncode(query) & rawUrlEncode(postData) & secret) with RFC-3986 encoding and only Authorization/X-Api-* headers signed; both add client_id/sign_method=md5/sign_time to the query, over https the signed query is replaced by client_id+client_secret, and unconfigured or failed calls return null so business services (OAuth token exchange, certificate issuing, lead capture) degrade.

The Shuyun open-platform gateway (ShuyunOpenGatewayClient, in ecshopx-shuyun) is the deliberate exception to fail-soft: it throws IllegalStateException on missing per-company config row and on non-2xx HTTP responses, because its listeners run on queued messages where the platform-default retry (3 attempts) is the correct behavior; it signs via Gateway-* headers (Gateway-Authid, Gateway-Sign, Gateway-Action-Method, Gateway-Request-Time, Gateway-Access-Token) with the per-company app_secret from company_shuyun_open_platform_config, and persists every call to a traffic-audit table.

Shuyun open-platform tokens are refreshed daily by TokenRefreshScheduler with @Scheduled(cron = "0 15 4 * * ?") (04:15, aligned with the PHP dailyAt('4:15')) against token-refresh-base-uri (default http://open-client.shuyun.com), with Shuyun calling back to store the new token; the fallbackGatewayAccessToken is deliberately empty by default so outbound calls are refused rather than sent unsigned.

Shuyun has two independent stacks: the legacy UAPI (ShuyunSignedGatewayClient in ecshopx-third-party, u_* query-param md5 signing, remaining uses member modify/unbind behind http-enabled flags, otherwise degrades at the business layer) and the open platform (ecshopx-shuyun, Gateway-* header signing, per-company config in company_shuyun_open_platform_config) — the ecshopx-shuyun package-info documents this split explicitly as 遗留 UAPI + 开放平台 open-api.

Youshu analytics integration stores credentials in the youshu_setting DB table (not Redis) and signs every call via YoushuOpenApiSignSupport: 32-char random nonce, epoch timestamp, sign=sha256, and signature = HMAC-SHA256(appSecret, sorted query string) in lowercase hex appended as query params; the data source is bootstrapped get-then-add against /data-api/v1/data_source.

WdtErp's pull side (WdtErpSyncService, driven by XxlJob handlers sync-wdt-inventory and sync-wdt-logistics) iterates `companysRedisTemplate.keys("WdtErpSetting:*")`, skips tenants without is_open=true, pages through Wdt's wait-sync lists, and writes results back into item stores and order shipment records, with promotion-aware inventory exclusion before overwriting stock.

System-link never reads order tables directly: payload assembly for Jushuitan order upload and WdtErp pushSelf/aftersale is declared as port interfaces in ecshopx-common/port/systemlink (JushuitanTradeFinishOrderUploadAssemblePort, WdtErpTradeFinishPushSelfAssemblePort, WdtErpTradeAfterSaleAssemblePort, WdtErpTradeCancelOrderAddAssemblePort, JushuitanAftersaleAddPayloadAssemblePort) and implemented in the data-owning modules (ecshopx-orders for trade finish; bootstrap for aftersales mapping) — the same dependency inversion the OpenAPI gateway uses.

The OME (Shopex ERP) client ShopexErpOpenApiClient lives in ecshopx-goods (service/ome) because goods import was its first consumer, and is configured by a single `ecshopx.ome.openapi-url` (empty in application.properties ⇒ fail_msg skip); it signs per tenant with double-MD5-upper over ShopexerpSetting Redis values and form-POSTs with flag/method/type=json/charset/ver/timestamp.

The WeChat customs declaration for cross-border orders lives in ecshopx-orders, not ecshopx-cross-border: TradeFinishCustomDeclareOrderBusService (trade-finish listener @Order 95) POSTs XML to https://api.mch.weixin.qq.com/cgi-bin/mch/customs/customdeclareorder only for pay_type=wxpay (point/deposit/membercard skipped), order.type != 0 (cross-border marker), present transaction_id, third_params customs code + merchant customs no, and non-empty identity_id/identity_name; it persists the result into custom_declare_order_result keyed by order_id, and every skip/failure path is a debug log so a cross-border order never fails its payment flow.

ecshopx-cross-border is settings-only CRUD with no outbound HTTP: three admin controllers over crossborder_set, crossborder_taxstrategy (TaxstrategyListService pages by company with state=1 and name LIKE filter), and crossborder_origincountry, all gated by CrossBorderShopRoutePermissionService.assertRouteAllowed (crossborder.* role-menu aliases with whitelists and a salesperson_workwechat bypass).

Aliyun SMS sign/template lifecycle is modeled as twelve dispatch jobs job:48–job:59 (Add/Modify/Delete/QuerySmsSign, AddSmsBatchRecord, QuerySendDetail, Add/Modify/Delete/QuerySmsTemplate, SyncSmsSigns, SyncSmsTemplates) registered in bootstrap configs via dispatchRegistry.registerJob, plus five XxlJob handlers polling audit status and send details; CompanySmsChannelRouter picks Aliyun vs Shuyun-OEM vs Shopex channel per company.

Alipay mini-program template messages (ecshopx-ali AliTemplateMsgService.send) go through the EasySDK Factory.Marketing.TemplateMessage().send guarded by a static SDK_LOCK because EasySDK options are process-global; templates resolve per company/scene from Redis `aliopen_template_library:{companyId}:{scenesName}`, and a future send_time_desc causes the publisher to enqueue with a delay so job:136 fires it later (re-checking the delay).

DispatchOptions.eventDefaults() is SYNC mode while jobDefaults() and the systemlink ERP publishers use ASYNC with Redis driver; SYNC-published events execute every registered listener in-process via the sync driver (order controlled by @Order on registration configs), while ASYNC+REDIS events queue one message per listener, decoupling the payment callback from slow ERPs.

Two OrdersTradeFinishDispatchPublisher beans exist in bootstrap: the @Primary one publishing event:291 (EVENT_TRADE_FINISH) and the named `ordersTradeFinishDispatchPublisherOfflineCsv292` publishing event:292 used by OfflinePaymentDoCheckService for offline bank-transfer approval; both wrap OrdersTradeFinishAfterCommitDispatchPublisher, deferring the publish until after commit when a transaction is active.

Module roles: ecshopx-system-link is the ERP connectivity domain (系统联通域) covering Jushuitan, WdtErp and OME; ecshopx-third-party is the third-party integration domain (第三方对接域) hosting Prism gateways, Marketing Center, DmCrm, Shopex CRM, SaasErp, Shuyun legacy UAPI, Dada/Shansong, AMap; ecshopx-youshu is the Youshu analytics domain (有数分析配置域); ecshopx-shuyun carries the Shuyun open-platform stack.

Per-tenant integration state lives outside static config: Redis keys on the companys template — JushuitanSetting:{sha1(companyId)}, WdtErpSetting:{sha1(companyId)}, ShopexerpSetting:{sha1(companyId)}, DmCrmSetting:{sha1(companyId)}, damo_token:{companyId}, aliopen_template_library:{companyId}:{scenesName} — plus DB tables company_shuyun_open_platform_config, youshu_setting, and openapi_developer (external_* fields feed Marketing Center); static properties carry only platform-level credentials.

ecshopx-digios integrates the DigiOS gateway (default base https://hobbits.ishopex.cn) via DigiOsProperties (prefix ecshopx.digios, enabled=false by default, six methods.* gateway paths, token path /gateway/token, stock-push-max-rows=200, adjustment doc types code_000008/code_000009); no ecshopx.digios.* keys appear in application.properties, and DigiOsConfigService.resolve merges the properties with a per-company digios_company_config DB row whose is_enabled=1 turns the integration on for that company and whose base_url/app_key/app_secret override the platform values.

DigiOsGatewayClient sends PUT/POST JSON with X-Auth-Client/X-Auth-Token/X-Message-Id headers, returns failed DigiOsGatewayResult values ("digios disabled" / "digios config incomplete") instead of throwing when unconfigured, treats 2xx without errorCode/errorMessage as success, and on a token-unauthorized response (401/403, errorCode MS-GATEWAY-0003, or a Token/Client ID message) clears the token cache, logs the failed attempt, and retries exactly once; every attempt is persisted to digios_api_log.

DigiOsTokenService caches access tokens on the sharedStringRedisTemplate under digios:token:{companyId}:{clientId} with TTL max(60, expire - tokenExpireSkewSeconds), serializes concurrent refreshes with a 10-second SETNX lock (lock losers sleep 200 ms and re-read the cache), fetches tokens by POSTing {clientId, appSecret} to {baseUrl}/gateway/token, throws IllegalStateException on fetch failure or an invalid response, and logs every token fetch to digios_api_log as method auth.token.

All DigiOS traffic — outbound gateway calls, token fetches, and the inbound stock push — is persisted to the digios_api_log table (indexed on (company_id, created) and method) with direction in/out, method, http_status, outcome, runtime_ms, JSON request/response bodies, and an error message truncated at 1024 characters.

ecshopx-bootstrap registers five async digios dispatch listeners on existing domain planes: distributor create event:263 (@Order 79) and update event:264 (@Order 80) for store profile/warehouse sync, operator create (@Order 81) for staff-only account upsert, normal order delivery (@Order 80) for the outbound stock adjustment, and the dedicated event:digios:aftersales_return_adjustment plane (@Order 81). The aftersales plane is published ASYNC+REDIS by bootstrap's DigiOsAftersalesReturnAdjustmentDispatchPublisherImpl, which AftersalesMerchantSendbackConfirmService (ecshopx-aftersales) invokes after commit when a merchant confirms a REFUND_GOODS send-back; the declared POS-store-account create listener name (`listener:digios.account_sync_on_pos_store_account_create`) is never registered — POS accounts sync through the synchronous PosStoreAccountDigiOsCreatePort gate and, on success, only an unlistened `event:companys:pos_store_account_create` event is published. ecshopx-common also carries NoopDigiOsAftersalesReturnAdjustmentDispatchPublisher in its mock package as a no-op fallback publisher.

Distributor create syncs the DigiOS store profile (PUT store.create; the returned numeric store id is saved to digios_store_mapping unique per (company_id, distributor_id)) and then upserts one warehouse plus two logic warehouses ({shop_code} 正品仓 typ 0 and {shop_code}-1 次品仓 typ 1); distributor update POSTs store.update with the mapped id and skips silently when no mapping row exists; payloads are refused when shop_code/name are missing, the area code cannot be resolved, or address/contact are empty.

DigiOsRegionMapper lazily loads digios_regions.json (configurable via ecshopx.digios.regions-json, default classpath:digios_regions.json) — a by_code tree of Chinese administrative codes with name/type/parent — and resolves a distributor's areaCd by preferring the deepest regions_id code, then falling back to name matching district→city→province with type filters and parent-chain disambiguation when a name maps to multiple codes.

DigiOS account sync is deliberately split (G-D1): the operator-create listener only syncs operator_type=staff operators through DigiOsAccountSyncService (PUT account.upsert, validating data.usrId/data.acc), while distributor/POS store accounts sync via syncCreatePos and are skipped when the mobile is empty (G-D3).

PosStoreAccountDigiOsCreatePort (common interface with a @Primary digios impl and a NoOp fallback) is invoked synchronously by PosStoreAccountWriteService/PosStoreAccountImportService before the local POS account row is inserted: when DigiOS is enabled it requires a mobile and upserts first, and any failure throws BadRequestException — blocking local creation (ECX-10668) — making this the one digios path that throws instead of failing soft.

DigiOsStoreAdjustmentSyncService pushes store-inventory adjustments on order delivery (outbound, docTypCd code_000008, nm = order id) and aftersales return (inbound, code_000009, only aftersales_type=REFUND_GOODS, nm = aftersales bn); DigiOsStoreAdjustmentLineResolver resolves lines via direct JdbcTemplate reads of orders/orders_delivery/aftersales_detail and the distributor's shop_code, details are chunked by stockPushMaxRows, each chunk PUTs store.adjustment, and unresolvable lines or a disabled config skip silently.

The inbound DigiOS stock push arrives through the OpenAPI gateway method ecx.digios.product.stock_push (DigiOsStockController in ecshopx-openapi), which delegates via the OpenapiDigiOsProductStockPushPort (common interface, impl in digios) to DigiOsStockPushService: it validates sku_list capped at stockPushMaxRows, resolves sku_id to items by item_bn and shop_code to distributors, applies stock through the same NormalGoodsStoreImportRowService.applyRow used by CSV store imports, reports not_find_sku/update_error, and logs the call to digios_api_log as an in entry.

The Shuyun open platform is also an inbound surface: three callback families (token, loyalty-grade, offline-benefit create/single-send/batch-send) are exposed on dual /api/v1 and /api/v1/third paths, and all of them pass through InboundSignedCallbackPreparer, which resolves the tenant (query/body appId, platCode, or a shadow benefitId lookup), then verifies an MD5 signature keyed by the platform-wide callback-identity-secret over sorted query params plus SY-Request-Time/callBackTime and optionally the raw JSON body (ECX-10841), and finally enforces a Redis replay guard (300 s skew, 600 s TTL) whose replays are detected by a SETNX on `shuyun:cb:replay:{sha256(sign|requestTime)}` with the request time accepted as seconds or milliseconds epoch; an empty callback-identity-secret rejects every callback.
